incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL), and Decree No. 2020-106 (simplified incorporation procedures)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) via the Guichet Unique (one-stop electronic portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) and the M0 form (now integrated into the Guichet Unique electronic filing)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum; capital may be €1 or higher. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid up in cash or in kind; for cash contributions, funds must be deposited in a blocked bank account (compte bloqué) until registration, then released to the company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the undersigned, being the sole shareholder of the SARL, hereby (1) subscribes to the entire share capital of €[amount] divided into [number] shares of €[par value] each, fully paid up; (2) adopts the Articles of Association as presented; (3) designates the registered office at [address]; (4) appoints [Name] as Manager (Gérant) for an indefinite term with full powers to act on behalf of the company; (5) authorizes the Manager to complete all formalities for registration, including publication of a legal notice and filing with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; and (6) ratifies all actions taken prior to this resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and Verify Availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) via the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the INPI database to ensure no identical or confusingly similar trademark or corporate name exists. Submit a name reservation request through the Guichet Unique; the name is reserved for 4 months. Provide the proposed name, activity description, and applicant details.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to conflict, file an appeal with the INPI or modify the name and resubmit. Alternatively, request a formal opinion from the INPI on distinctiveness.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (if real estate contribution or special provisions) or private drafting with legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statuts in French, including company name, registered office, corporate purpose (offshore wind turbine pilings installation), share capital, share classes, management structure, and governance rules. If any contribution is in kind (e.g., equipment), a commissaire aux apports (contribution auditor) must be appointed. Notarization is mandatory if real property is contributed or if the company is a SARL de famille; otherwise, private signature is acceptable.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate of capital deposit (attestation de dépôt de fonds)
Identity documents of shareholders and managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the Articles, correct the deficiencies and resubmit. For notarized documents, the notary will handle corrections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Share Capital in Blocked Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any French bank or regulated financial institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary bank account in the company's name (or in the name of the founders) and deposit the full amount of cash contributions. Obtain a certificate of deposit (attestation de blocage) from the bank, which will be released upon registration. The certificate must state the amount, the account holder, and the blocking condition.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the deposit, provide additional KYC documents or choose another bank. The certificate is valid for 3 months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish a Legal Notice in a Journal of Legal Notices (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any authorized legal gazette (e.g., Les Affiches Parisiennes, Le Bulletin Officiel des Annonces Civiles et Commerciales - BODACC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft a notice containing the company name, legal form (SARL), share capital, registered office, corporate purpose, manager's name, and the registry where the company will be registered. Publish the notice in a JAL in the department of the registered office. Obtain a certificate of publication (attestation de parution).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL rejects the notice due to incomplete information, correct and resubmit. The publication is valid for 6 months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Dossier with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (via Guichet Unique electronic portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete dossier through the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr). The dossier includes the Articles of Association, bank certificate, publication certificate, manager's acceptance, and identification documents. Pay the filing fee (approx. €75). The registry will review and issue a Kbis extract (official registration certificate) upon approval.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office address (lease or ownership)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the registry will issue a 'demande de complément' (request for additional information). Correct the deficiencies within 15 days. If rejected, appeal to the President of the Commercial Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INSEE (for SIREN/SIRET), URSSAF (social security), and Tax Office (DGFiP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Kbis extract, the company is automatically registered with INSEE (SIREN number) and tax authorities. The manager must register for social security (URSSAF) and obtain a company health insurance number. If the company will employ staff, register as an employer. Also, open a permanent bank account and transfer the blocked funds.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration with URSSAF is delayed, contact the local URSSAF office. For tax registration, the DGFiP will issue a VAT number automatically.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de la Transition Écologique (Ministry of Ecological Transition) - Direction Générale de l'Énergie et du Climat (DGEC) and Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation Environnementale Unique (Unique Environmental Authorization) for offshore wind installation activities, and a specific permit for marine works (Titre de travaux maritimes) if in territorial waters

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autorité Environnementale (Environmental Authority) within the CGEDD (Conseil Général de l'Environnement et du Développement Durable)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full EIA Report (Étude d'impact) required for offshore wind turbine foundation installation, as it falls under Annex I of the Environmental Code (Code de l'environnement) - Category 1: Installations for the production of energy from renewable sources in the marine environment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Water Framework Directive (2000/60/EC) and the Marine Strategy Framework Directive (2008/56/EC). Wastewater discharges must meet the thresholds in the French Water Law (Code de l'environnement, Art. R.214-1). VOC emissions from marine diesel engines must comply with the EU Directive 2016/802 (sulphur content) and the IMO MARPOL Annex VI. Waste handling must follow the Waste Management Plan (Plan de gestion des déchets) and the French Decree on waste (Code de l'environnement, Art. R.541-1).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours (SDIS) for any onshore facilities. Structural load inspections for cranes and heavy equipment must be performed by a certified body (e.g., Bureau Veritas, APAVE). Occupational health and safety clearance from the CARSAT (Caisse d'Assurance Retraite et de la Santé au Travail) and compliance with the Labor Code (Code du travail) for workplace safety, including a risk assessment (Document Unique).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP) via the official portal impots.gouv.fr; VAT registration and corporate formalities coordinated through the Guichet Unique Électronique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; SIREN/SIRET identifiers issued by INSEE through the SIRENE national registry.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SARL, incorporation documents are filed with the Guichet Unique (Business Formalities Centre), which transmits registration data to INSEE for allocation of a SIREN company number and SIRET establishment number. The DGFIP then issues an intra-Community VAT number (Numéro de TVA Intracommunautaire) prefixed FR, ordinarily notified by post and via the online impots.gouv.fr account within approximately two to four weeks. A non-EU parent without a French establishment that performs taxable supplies in France must register directly with the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) for VAT and may be required to appoint an accredited tax representative under Article 289A of the Code Général des Impôts (CGI), unless the representative obligation is waived. The applicant must submit extract of registration from home jurisdiction, evidence of economic activity, domestic VAT certificate or equivalent, and identity documentation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL is taxable at entity level on corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, IS) by default. Small and medium-sized SARLs satisfying the size and ownership conditions of Article 239 bis AA CGI may elect for a limited five-year period to be taxed on shareholders under the income tax regime (Impôt sur le Revenu). A SARL may also join a French fiscal group (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI as a fully owned subsidiary of a French-resident parent, allowing tax consolidation of group profits and losses. Domestic law does not provide a US-style check-the-box election; hybrid mismatch consequences are addressed under the ATAD 1 rules codified in Articles 212 bis and 209 B CGI, including anti-arbitrage adjustments for inverted hybrids and double deduction arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For an established French SARL, the VAT exemption threshold is €85,000 for the principal supply of goods and €34,400 for services (2024 thresholds under Article 293 B CGI), but once the supply involves installation, configuration or works connected with real property, the service-related services threshold of €34,400 generally applies. A legal person carrying on a taxable economic activity in France must register if taxable turnover exceeds these thresholds. Non-established foreign suppliers have no registration threshold: any taxable transaction in France, unless subject to reverse charge in B2B context for certain services or simplified IOSS for distance sales, requires a French VAT number.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France has introduced a mandatory e-invoicing reform for domestic B2B transactions: from 1 July 2026 all VAT-registered taxpayers must be able to receive electronic invoices through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or an accredited private dematerialisation platform, and e-emitting obligations apply from the same date for medium and large enterprises; small and medium enterprises are phased in by 1 July 2027. Required standards are Factur-X, UBL, or UBL 2.1/UNTD. E-reporting transmits transaction data to DGFIP for VAT reconciliation in near real-time via API. Tax clearance is not a wholesale pre-authorisation system; however export declarations are processed through the French Customs DELTA system using real-time interoperability, and public-sector invoicing to French government entities already mandates Factur-X via Chorus Pro. Invoices for intra-Community supplies must appear in the recapitulative EC Sales List; foreign persons with French VAT numbers must observe the same e-reporting procedures.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under CGI Article 262-I to physical exports of goods transported directly outside the European Union by the supplier or the purchaser, provided the goods leave France accompanied by a customs export declaration in DELTA. French-established suppliers may also zero-rate intra-Community supplies under Article 262-II when the purchaser provides a valid EU VAT number and a transport document proves movement to another Member State; such supplies must be reported on the EC Sales List. For offshore wind turbine pilings, if the monopiles are incorporated into an immovable foundation affixed to the seabed in France, the supply and installation is generally treated as a supply of goods with installation with the place of taxation in France, subject to 20% VAT, unless the contract demonstrably transfers risks and title to the goods before installation and the goods are exported as movables. Services physically rendered in France and directly linked to goods that will be exported may qualify for zero-rating where expressly provided by French administrative doctrine, provided the services are performed for a customer established outside the EU and the goods are subsequently transported outside France or the EU. Exporters must retain proof of export and evidence of direct shipment; VAT credit/refunds are claimed via the foreign VAT refund procedure (EU Directive 2008/9/CE for EU-established claimants or the EU 13th Directive refund for non-EU claimants) or through the periodic VAT return (CA3) in connection with the French SARL's export activity.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: French Customs and DGFIP jointly audit export zero-rating claims. Fraudulent claims or artificial export structures trigger immediate reassessment of VAT, with a 40% penalty for substantial inaccurate declarations under Article 1728 CGI and an 80% bad-faith penalty plus potential 40% additional penalty for abusive manipulation under Article 1729 CGI. Interest at 0.20% per month accrues from the original due date. Customs proceedings under the French Customs Code Articles 414 and 425 may impose fines of up to two times the evaded VAT or value of the goods, confiscation of the goods and transport, and suspension of the economic operator's customs authorisations. In criminal cases, false export declarations carry penalties of up to five years imprisonment and €450,000 fines. Retroactive clawbacks may be raised for up to six years from the tax year (extended to ten years for hidden operations), and administrative tolerance is limited where the exporter fails to produce the mandatory customs documentation bundle or cannot demonstrate repatriation of foreign exchange within the statutory deadline.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France and Direction Générale du Trésor
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full convertibility for both current and capital accounts with no exchange controls. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted following corporate tax compliance and beneficial ownership verification. Hurdles are minimal for EU-domiciled entities and standard cross-border project finance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds under French law. Exporters may retain foreign currency receipts in bank accounts without conversion to euros. Statutory requirements focus solely on accurate customs declarations and invoicing via the Single Administrative Document (SAD).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility via authorized EMI providers integrated with French banking rails, subject to strict compliance with the French Monetary and Financial Code and Payment Services Directive (PSD2). Offshore digital EMIs require local partner validation and ongoing regulatory reporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote KYC and video interview permitted for standard corporate onboarding; physical presence required only for high-risk or complex structures upon bank request.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kbis extract from French commercial registry, share capital certificates, and board resolutions confirming ownership percentages
Detailed ownership chart and source of funds documentation

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'CAP' for capital injections or 'EQTY' for equity. Verification includes board resolutions, shareholder agreements, and beneficial ownership declarations. French banks process euro-denominated wires to local IBAN accounts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails include SWIFT MT103 for direct payments and Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) under UCP 600 for project financing. For offshore wind turbine pilings, use escrow accounts with project-specific purpose codes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Currency swaps and cross-currency basis swaps

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Deposit, Members' Approval Record, and Management Report Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) at the Company's registered-office jurisdiction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' approval meeting within six months after fiscal year-end; deposit with the Registrar within one month after approval; calendar-year SARL typically approved by 30 June and deposited by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil fine of up to EUR 3,000 for the legal entity; court-ordered coercive payment (astreinte) obtainable by any interested party; persistent default triggers Registrar formal notice and administrative strike-off (radiation) proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Liasse Fiscale: Forms 2065 and 2050 Series) and Balance-Sheet Tax Attachments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French General Directorate of Public Finances (DGFiP) – Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) having jurisdiction over the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 3 May of the year following the close of a calendar-year fiscal period; mandatory electronic filing; deadline adjusted to the next business day when 3 May is not a business day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing increase of 10%; increase to 40% when filed within 30 days after formal assessment notice and to 80% for deliberate concealment or abusive conduct; late-payment monthly interest of 0.20%; late-payment additions of 10% rising to 20%, followed by tax lien enforcement and forced collection

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation Declaration (Confirmation Annuelle de la Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days following expiry of the twelve-month period from the most recent beneficial-owner declaration filing; any transfer of shares or change in control requires an updated declaration within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of up to EUR 15,000 for natural persons and EUR 75,000 for the legal entity; imprisonment of up to six months for knowingly false or incomplete declarations; the Commercial Court may suspend the Company's standing to bring proceedings until regularisation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Local Business Contribution Declaration and Payment (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises – CFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP – Local Tax Collection Office (Comptable Public) and Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Declaration and payment due by 15 December of the tax year, determined by reference to the 1 January taxable position and the prior-year rental values
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment addition of 5% and statutory monthly late interest of 0.20%; compulsory recovery proceedings, garnishment, and attachment of bank accounts upon continued non-payment

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory for the SARL when two of the three following thresholds are exceeded at the fiscal year-end: balance sheet total above EUR 4,000,000; net turnover (exclusive of tax) above EUR 8,000,000; average number of permanent employees above 50. The audit is also mandatory when shareholders holding at least one-third of the corporate capital validly petition the Commercial Court, in control or consolidation scenarios, and by specific legal or contractual requirements
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory annual accounts must be prepared in accordance with the French Plan Comptable Général (PCG), French GAAP, and the règlements of the Autorité des Normes Comptables (ANC), transposing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as adopted by the European Union is permitted for consolidated financial statements but is not mandatory for the standalone SARL

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The legal representative of the SARL must file annually, within 30 days after expiry of the 12-month period following the most recent declaration, a confirmation declaration attesting to the accuracy of the beneficial-owner information held by the Registry. A transfer of parts sociales is perfected against the Company by signature of a written transfer instrument, inscription in the share-transfer register, and notification or acknowledgment by the gérant; any resulting change in the identity, shareholding percentage, or control of beneficial owners requires an updated UBO declaration within 30 days. The annual confirmation is not notarised and is filed electronically or directly at the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members' Decisions (Registre des décisions des associés) containing unanimous resolutions, ordinary and extraordinary shareholders' meetings, and appointment records
Register of Share Transfers and Ownership Interests (Registre des mouvements de titres) recording every transfer, pledge, or transmission of parts sociales
Corporate Minute Book (Registre des procès-verbaux d'assemblées et délibérations) with signed minutes, attendance sheets, and approving documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 – USD 2,400 per year for registered-office services and corporate legal secretarial maintenance in France
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – USD 11,000 per year for a statutory audit engagement of a mid-capitalisation SARL in the offshore installation sector

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard rate (art. 219 CGI) effective from FY 2022; a reduced 15% rate applies to the first €42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying small enterprises (turnover ≤ €10m). A 3.3% 'contribution sociale sur les bénéfices' (art. 235 ter ZC CGI) applies to the portion of IS exceeding €763,000, producing a marginal effective rate of 25.83%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for offshore wind installation. Available preferential products: CIR research tax credit (30% on R&D up to €100m, 5% beyond), CII innovation credit for SMEs (20%, capped €400k), JEI 'young innovative company' full exemption to €100k profit plus social charges exemptions, and regional/zones franches exemptions. Marine-renewable construction assets remain eligible for standard tax depreciation; no special super-deduction for monopile assets unless qualified under the 'utilisation de la production d'énergies renouvelables' financing rules (art. 217 quinquies CGI).
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward (art. 209 CGI) but utilisation is capped at the greater of €1,000,000 or 50% of the taxable profit exceeding €1,000,000 per fiscal year (deduction of the first €1,000,000 is always full). The 1-year carryback (report en arrière, art. 220 CGI) is limited to €1,000,000 and creates a créance d'IS recoverable over five years.
